amara.text: How did you end up needing to file a German tax return this year?

A colleague told me over lunch. I was between jobs last year, five months on Arbeitslosengeld I, and apparently once you've had more than about €410 of that in a year, filing stops being optional. I had no idea. I've been in Germany four years and this is my first return, so my first reaction wasn't "okay, a form", it was "am I already late? Is there a letter about me somewhere?"
What scares you most about it?

Getting it wrong in a system I can't read. There's a letter from the Agentur für Arbeit in my drawer, a Leistungsnachweis, that says my benefit data was sent to the Finanzamt. So they already know. That's the scary part, not the maths: they have the numbers and I don't. And the same colleague said the benefit can push up the tax on my salary even though the benefit itself was tax-free. I still don't understand how tax-free money makes a tax bill. I'm bracing for a number I can't size.
You said you tried an expert service before. What happened?

The app said an expert would get in touch within two days. Three weeks later, nothing, and every support chat repeated the same line. When a draft finally came back I honestly couldn't tell what the expert had done that the app hadn't. Then the price turned out to be a percentage of the refund, which I only really understood at that point, so I closed the account before anything was filed. I don't mind paying. I mind paying to be ghosted and then not being able to see the work.
When you signed up this time, what did you expect to happen next?

Honestly? Silence. That's what "signed up" has meant so far. What I wanted was a short list: here are the five things we need, here is what each one looks like, here is who you're dealing with, here is when you'll hear back. I Googled "Lohnsteuerbescheinigung" at eleven at night and got four forum answers that disagreed. If the app had just shown me a picture of it I'd have been done in ten minutes.
What would make you close the app and not come back?

A countdown. If you show me a red timer to 31 July I will freeze and "do it this weekend", which means never. Also a dead end: if I don't have a document and the only option is to upload it, I'm stuck on that one item and the whole thing stalls. And a chat window with nobody visibly behind it. I'm a PM, I know what an unstaffed chat looks like.
How do you feel about paying, and when would you want to pay?

I'll pay a flat price for a named person. I won't pay before I've seen that a person exists and has actually looked at my stuff. Tell me the price before I start, tell me again before I approve the return, and charge me after I've approved it. The percentage-of-refund thing felt like a trick even if it wasn't one, because I couldn't see the number until the end.
If you could change one thing about how these services treat first-time filers, what would it be?

Tell me the five things you need, tell me when you have them, and stop making me guess whether anyone is there. Everything else, the German words, the deadline, the money, I can handle if those three are true. Right now the anxiety isn't the tax. It's the not-knowing.

anna.text: Why did you join the Taxfix Expert Service network?

Pipeline. Straightforward employee returns, no acquisition cost. Under the fee schedule a €50,000 return is worth about €456 at the middle rate; a platform case is priced for the client at €99.99 minimum, so my share only works if the case closes in two touches. That is the whole calculation. It is fine work if the tooling protects those two touches and bad work if it doesn't.
What does a bad day look like?

July. My own return is due 31 July, my clients' are due 1 March next year, and half of them will still send everything in the last week. My job ad for a second Steuerfachangestellte has been open seven months; 72 percent of firms in this profession say the same, so it is not me. A bad day is thirty open cases and no way to tell, without opening each one, which of them I can actually work on. Then a client sends a Lohnsteuerbescheinigung as a sideways photo with page two missing and I spend three touches getting page two.
What do clients get wrong most often?

They think I have everything. Nobody told them what "everything" is, so they send what they have and wait. Then they treat any open text box as a hotline. Neither is their fault. It is the tool's fault for asking an open question and calling it intake. Give them a list with reasons and a picture of each document, and most of the chasing disappears.
What would make a follow-up cheap for you?

A queue that tells the truth and a request the client can act on without calling me. If I flag a document I want one click, a reason the client understands, blurry, wrong year, page missing, and the client fixing it on their own. That is one touch. Anything that turns into a conversation at sixty cases destroys the margin and puts my name on messages written at speed.
The consumer side wants to see what you checked before they approve. Is that a problem for you?

The opposite. I am legally accountable for what I file, so I want the client to approve after seeing it, and I want what they see to be what I actually verified, not a fixed claim made in my name. What I will not accept is a Verify button next to a document the tool never shows me. That is not a missing feature; that is the product asking me to carry a legal risk on its behalf.
Clients on review sites say things like "the partner firm was incompetent, it took six weeks". How do you read that?

I read it as: a document request went unanswered and nobody told either side the case was stuck. Six weeks is what silence looks like from the outside. It is rarely incompetence; it is a case sitting in a queue with four of six documents missing and no visible state on either end. If the client could see "waiting on you: two items" and I could see "stalled nine days", most of those reviews would not exist.
What would make you recommend the platform to another Steuerberaterin, and what would make you quit it in July?

Recommend: a morning triage that answers "what can I work on right now" in five seconds, structured requests with templates in my own voice, and a status I can trust, so "ready" means everything required is there and legible. Quit: anything that turns me into a hotline, anything that makes me certify what I have not seen, and any queue that does not sort by deadline in July. I do not need it to be pleasant. I need it to be honest and fast.
